To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the outcome of patients treated by haemodialysis for acute renal failure was related to age and severity of illness, and that a scoring system based on these factors was useful in predicting outcome.
the severity of acute renal failure in patients admitted to the ICU is associated with a high mortality rate.
the severity of illness on referral for continuous haemofliltration is a good predictor of outcome in acute renal failure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the relationship between the severity of acute renal failure and the use of renal replacement therapy.
the study of the effects of haemofiltrate on the function of the kidney, and the study of haemofilters.
the development and evaluation of a scoring system which is based on the clinical and laboratory findings of patients with acute oliguric renal failure.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of continuous haemofliltration in the ICU is associated with a 53% survival rate, which is improved over that of historical controls.
a scoring system based on five easily available variables can be used to assess prognosis at the time of initiation of haemofiltraton in acute renal failure.

the outcome of patients with acute tubular necrosis can be predicted by a scoring system based on age, need for ventilation, use of vasoactive drugs, urine output, serum bilirubine and serum creatinine, but that this system is not sufficiently accurate to be of use in the management of individual patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the severity of illness in acute renal failure is related to outcome.
the severity of illness on referral to the ICU was the most important factor determining outcome.
the severity of acute renal failure is related to outcome, but is not the only factor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of the scoring system to predict outcome is not as good as we would like it to be, but that the use of such a system is better than not using one at all.
a scoring system based on simple variables at the time of admission can be used to predict survival in patients with acute renal injury treated with continuous haemofliltration.

the outcome for acute renal failure patients treated on the intensive care unit with continuous renal replacement therapy has improved over the last few years and that outcome can be predicted at the time of presentation with a scoring system based on readily available clinical and laboratory variables.
